scene: A freshly tossed Turkish roka salad (rocket/arugula, pomegranate and white brined cheese) in ONE shallow matte ivory ceramic bowl, warm ivory background. Three-quarter view, landscape3:2, tight appetizing food portrait, the salad itself fills most of the frame. A low airy mound of real tender ROCKET leaves, narrow elongated5–8cm leaves with asymmetric deeply cut pointed lobes and delicate short stems. Leaves gently curl, overlap and bend in DIFFERENT natural directions, a few lifted edges and visible negative gaps; no stiff upright forest, identical oak-leaf stamps or mechanically flat green carpet. Ruby pomegranate arils are SMALL realistic5–8mm translucent angular droplets, about one tenth the length of a rocket leaf, loosely scattered with a few tucked between leaves; roughly25–35 clearly readable arils, never grape-sized spheres or perfect candy jewels. White brined cheese is broken into modest irregular1–2cm flakes and chunks with simple torn edges, dispersed naturally among the leaves, never huge evenly spaced white cubes. Optional walnuts appear ONLY as a few small roughly BROKEN tan fragments with one or two simple creases, never whole paired kernels or brain-like beads. Ingredients look lightly dressed with a thin olive-oil/lemon sheen, absolutely no puddle, dense gloss, invented herbs, onion, citrus slices, bread or extra garnish. Natural asymmetrical serving, ingredients lightly mixed rather than aligned like icons. Thin warm-brown outlines, broad clean MATTE two/three-tone cel shading, a few soft shadows to separate leaves, minimal internal leaf veins. Warm muted greens, ruby red and creamy white. No photographic microtexture, glossy3D/plastic materials, speckles, fractal crumbs or tiny repeated details. No turquoise or blue anywhere. No hands, text, labels, arrows, diagram or inset.
prompt:
Use case: style-transfer / scientific-educational. Redraw as premium Hayao Miyazaki-inspired hand-drawn Japanese animation culinary instruction art, consistent with the site's onigiri illustration reference: thin warm-brown ink contours, expressive but anatomically precise adult hands, clean matte two/three-tone cel shading, softly painted warm ivory background, muted peach skin, deep coral-red tuna, creamy white rice with a few dozen clean individually outlined grains, subtle pale honey wood only where a tabletop is needed. Clearly an animated illustration, NEVER photorealistic. No skin pores, fingerprints, photographic textures, glossy skin, 3D CGI, plastic rendering, geometric diagram hands, grids, labels, text, numbers or watermarks. Keep the food small and plausible, the instructional contacts precise, all hands anatomically complete with exactly one thumb plus four fingers, connected naturally; no extra/fused/missing digits. Use readable clear negative spaces. Orange arrows/dots only for pressure/contact; blue arcs only for motion when specified. Landscape 3:2 for steps/hero; square for ingredient cards. No text, no labels, no lettering, no watermark, no people, no animals or characters.

Rules: smooth, clean surfaces with crisp, well-defined outlines — no grain, noise, hatching, stippling, paper or crackle texture anywhere. Draw only what the scene names; nothing carried over from other steps. Food is in exactly the state the scene describes — nothing cooked, assembled or garnished ahead of time. Cooked egg is silky and glossy in soft folds, never curdled, foamy or pebbly; simmering liquid is smooth with only a few clean bubbles; rice is a soft mound with a modest number of clearly drawn grains. Cuts, sizes and quantities exactly as described and realistic. When a hand steadies food during knife work, it uses a proper claw grip (guiding fingertips tucked under, knuckles against the blade). A chicken thigh fillet is small and thin — about palm-sized (12 × 8 cm), 1–2 cm thick, irregular, pale pink with a little white fat — never a big thick slab, never marbled red like pork or beef. Hands belong to one right-handed cook seen from their own position: the right hand does the knife/chopsticks/pouring work from the right side of the frame, the left hand steadies or holds the pan handle from the left; keep the camera angle the same across a recipe's pictures. Prefer a tight close-up where the subject fills the frame. Every hand has exactly five digits: one thumb and four fingers of anatomically proportional lengths (middle longest, index and ring similar, little shortest), correct joints and thumb side. Fingers may be naturally occluded but never fused, added, elongated or truncated. Safe knife claw grip; blade cannot intersect fingers. One right-handed cook, consistent camera and vessels. Tight close-up showing the actual action and cut size. For rocking-chopping nuts, a free hand may safely rest on the blunt knife spine near the tip; never on the sharp edge.
